plan.title: feat(plan-sequence): keep the ordered plan current under the bound pre-push gate (advance on scope:complete, completion PR inherits entry, sanctioned unplanned-fix insert)

narratives.Description: Under the bound pre-push gate the ordered plan needs hand edits after almost every story: a finished entry stays current, and an unplanned fix has no sanctioned way in. This story derives the plan cursor from completed briefs wherever the plan is read, so the plan moves on when the completed brief arrives. It adds `plan-sequence:insert`, which needs a single-use operator grant minted at a terminal, and guards replace and clear with the same grant class when `plan.policy.requireBoundPrePrPush` is true (operator ruling 6906744687). Completion-PR admission is out of scope and carried on #6303.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator running the bound pre-push gate, I want the ordered plan to move on by itself when a story's brief is completed, and a sanctioned, attributable way to insert an unplanned fix, so that I stop hand-editing `.deft/plan-sequence.json` after every story.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/plan-sequence/derive.ts: `derivePlanCursor` (issue and story-id keys only; completed origin = finished; cancelled or failed origin = terminal-lifecycle stop; no-origin entry follows the stored cursor) and `materializeDerivedCursor`. Use it in `verifyPlanTarget` (types.ts); the #4129 drift text in terminal-drift.ts keeps the operator stop for the cancelled case only.
2. types.ts: new closed top-level key `insert_approvals` (rows of entry_id, grant_id, approved_at) in the closed shape and the parser; entry keys unchanged.
3. packages/core/src/plan-sequence/approval-grant.ts: one template `plan-sequence-approval` minted only through mintHumanOriginGrant into the main clone store, bound to repo, sequence_id, generation and action (insert kind:id, issue and position; replace; clear), single-use; find, claim and roll back on a failed write with returned failures.
4. packages/core/src/plan-sequence/complete-advance.ts plus a hook in packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts: after a successful complete, write the stored cursor forward only for an untracked plan in the same checkout and print one named line; never fail or roll back the completion.
5. packages/runtime/src/plan-sequence.ts: current, advance and the new insert verb derive first; set on an existing plan and clear need the grant only when requireBoundPrePrPush is true; verify-plan-sequence.ts prints the approval row. Wire the template in authz.ts, the verb in dispatch.ts, route-argv.ts and tasks/plan-sequence.yml.
6. Skills: remove the CLEAN-time advance for entries that have a brief from the pre-pr and review-cycle skills (and the preamble and commands.md); refresh the skills pack and RULE-MAP; content-contract test.
7. Tests for every case in the Bound test list, plus one disposable consumer fixture that runs complete, next-story push, approved insert and fix push through the real pre-PR controller and pre-push gate; tests mint through the core mint seam, never a real terminal mint. One CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] line.

narratives.Overview:
1. Derived cursor: wherever the plan is read (`plan-sequence:current`, `verify:plan-sequence`, every plan verb before it writes), an entry is finished when it is marked completed or when its lifecycle origin, matched by the issue and story-id keys of `resolvePlanEntryLifecycleOrigin` (never by title alone), is a brief in `completed/` in that checkout. The effective current entry is the first pending entry from the stored cursor on that is not finished; when none remains the plan is effectively exhausted. An entry whose origin is in `cancelled/` stops with `terminal-lifecycle`, as #4129 does today. An entry with no lifecycle origin follows the stored cursor.
2. No second record: `scope:complete` and `scope:cancel` never depend on the plan and are never rolled back for it. After a completion, `scope:complete` writes the stored cursor forward only when its own checkout holds an untracked plan, never a tracked plan or another checkout's plan, and prints one named line (`advanced`, `derived-only`, `no-sequence`, `no-entry`, `not-current`, `store-failed`). A failed write changes nothing else, because readers derive.
3. One advance owner: the CLEAN-time `plan-sequence:advance` step leaves the review-cycle and pre-pr skills for entries that have a brief. The #4129 remediation text keeps the operator stop for the cancelled case only.
4. Approved insert: `plan-sequence:insert` adds one pending entry at the effective cursor or at a named later index. It needs a human-origin grant minted on a TTY through the existing `authz:grant` machinery (one new template), bound to the repository, `sequence_id`, generation, entry kind and id, and position, and usable once. It writes an approval row (entry id, grant id, time) under one new closed top-level key; entry keys are unchanged. `verify:plan-sequence` prints that row for the current entry.
5. No unapproved chain: `plan-sequence:set` in a checkout that already holds a plan file (live or exhausted) and `plan-sequence:clear` need the same grant class. A first `set` in a checkout with no plan file is unchanged.
6. Tests: a completed brief with a stale stored cursor; a store failure during completion; a tracked plan (never written by completion); a linked worktree with no plan; a cancelled origin; a title-only match (not finished); a manual advance after a derived advance; an insert without a grant, with a grant for another entry or position, and with a reused grant; advance to exhaustion then `set` without a grant; `clear` without a grant. One disposable consumer fixture with the bound pre-push gate enrolled runs complete, next-story push, approved insert and fix push through the real pre-PR controller and pre-push gate.

## In plain English
A consumer project reported that keeping the ordered plan (`.deft/plan-sequence.json`) current cost more than the delivery work: 82 plan-sequence commands in two days. Three routine updates have no supported command. A finished entry stays current until someone advances it. A completion PR has no entry of its own. A bug fix that is not in the plan has no sanctioned way in. The open question is which mechanism closes each gap without turning the plan into something an agent can rewrite to admit its own work.

## Pains
- P1 — A finished plan entry stays current until someone advances it by hand, so the next story's pre-PR pass and push are refused.
- P2 — A completion (leftover-complete or lifecycle) PR for issue N is not admitted under the plan entry for issue N; it needs a separate entry or a hand edit.
- P3 — An unplanned fix is refused, and there is no sanctioned, attributable way for the operator to insert it. The routes used today are hand edits to the plan, or a human commit outside the agent.

## Notes for the arc
- This repository runs with `requireBoundPrePrPush: false` (#6024; re-enabling is tracked on #6025). A fix cannot be field-tested here. The lean must say how it will be verified.
- Tracked elsewhere and outside this warrant: plan-only commit with no active brief (#5839), parallel cohort entries (#4433), `pre-pr:run` as one command (#5933, #5977).

## Operator launch
Relayed by the dispatching session, not typed in this session. Scott answered "Yes, arcs only" to the question "Start a third-clone session that runs arcs only for the next wave?". Standing steer, verbatim: "you can yolo them and start implementation when they land". This session runs the arc only: no ingest, no brief, no code, no PR.

## In plain English

The issue asks to advance the ordered plan when a story completes, admit its completion PR under the original entry, and provide an approved way to insert unplanned fixes. The pinned code already supports manual advancement and guarded plan writes; the missing work is their integration with completion and authorization. The proposal needs explicit rules for completion after the cursor advances, interrupted updates, and approval provenance before it can bind. Verification was read-only at dispatch SHA `1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04`; no tests were executed.

### 1. Completion inheritance must survive advancement without admitting unrelated work — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/plan-sequence/types.ts:291–342` verifies only the current entry and rejects exhausted sequences before matching. Advancement at line 375 changes the current index or marks the sequence exhausted. Ask 2 and comment 6857544678 require completion PR inheritance.

**Failure mode:** Completing A advances the cursor to B, so A’s subsequent lifecycle PR still fails. Completing the final entry produces the same failure through exhaustion. Conversely, admitting any PR that mentions an issue anywhere in the plan would authorize new product changes under old completed entries.

**Disposition:** Bind a narrow completion admission branch that resolves the repository-qualified issue and brief continuity, proves the lifecycle-only change, and permits the relevant completed entry even after advancement or exhaustion. Preserve current-entry checking for product work. Existing lifecycle path classification in `packages/core/src/check/session-completed-ac.ts:29–56` is useful inventory, but path membership alone does not prove that edits belong to the claimed issue. Require negative cases for unrelated product changes and another issue’s lifecycle changes, alongside the requested no-entry case.

### 2. “Same operation” needs recoverable, exactly-once advancement — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/plan-sequence/store.ts:258` uses a sidecar lock for plan mutation, with generation mismatch and persistence failures defined at lines 28–36. `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts:1020–1054` separately publishes and rolls back lifecycle state. Its completed-brief restamp path writes again at line 1392.

**Failure mode:** Appending an advance after completion can leave a completed brief with a stale cursor when persistence fails. Advancing first can release the next story before completion succeeds. Retrying completion or restamping an already completed brief must not advance a second entry. A concurrent insertion can also invalidate the entry observed before completion.

**Disposition:** Bind reuse of the existing generation/lock mechanism plus an explicit recoverable completion-to-entry association. Require failure-injection coverage between durable writes, retry idempotency, and stale-generation refusal without consuming another entry. A simple sequential call is attractive because it is small, but becomes sufficient only if the surrounding operation demonstrably supplies rollback or recovery across both records.

### 3. Approval must authorize the specific insertion, not merely record an actor — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `content/docs/scope-provenance.md:73` expressly rejects `authorized_by` and head-authored confirmations as consent. Existing operator mint infrastructure is documented in `packages/runtime/src/authz.ts:19–26` and imported from `human-presence-mint` at line 65.

**Failure mode:** An agent-callable insertion command with `--approved-by` or `--confirm` can manufacture its own permission. Even genuine approval becomes reusable for different work if it is not bound to the inserted target and ordered-plan mutation.

**Disposition:** Bind the existing human-presence approval machinery to a specific repository, sequence identity/generation, entry identity, and insertion position; have verification validate that association. Specify how existing set/replace routes interact with this requirement so replacing the plan cannot bypass the new approval check. Prefer reuse over a parallel consent system. A forge-backed mechanism could replace local minting if it supplies equally explicit identity and mutation binding.

## In plain English
Problem: keeping the ordered plan current costs more than the delivery work. A finished entry stays current until someone advances it. A completion PR has no entry of its own. An unplanned fix has no approved way into the plan. The first lean made `scope:complete` write the plan forward and tried to keep the brief's folder and the stored cursor in step. Solution this lean proposes: stop keeping two records in step. A brief that sits in the completed folder counts as a finished plan entry wherever the plan is read, so the cursor moves when the brief moves and nothing has to be advanced by hand. The stored cursor only catches up, and only in a plan file that is not tracked in git. A completion PR is admitted under the entries of the briefs it completes, and it is recognised from the change set itself: briefs that move to the completed folder with their content unchanged, plus the CHANGELOG and the ledger, and nothing else. An unplanned fix enters through one insert command that needs an approval the operator mints at a terminal for that one entry and position; replacing or clearing an existing plan needs the same approval, so no chain of unapproved commands can add an entry. What this does not do: it does not make the plan file tamper-proof (marker A1), and it does not turn the bound pre-push gate back on in this repository (#6025). If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design, as three stories. There is no leftover next-build.

## Bound remedy
1. Derived cursor. Wherever the plan is read (`plan-sequence:current`, `verify:plan-sequence`, and every plan verb before it writes), an entry is finished when it is marked completed, or when its lifecycle origin is a brief in `completed/` in that checkout. The origin is matched by the issue and story-id keys of `resolvePlanEntryLifecycleOrigin`, never by title alone. The effective current entry is the first pending entry, from the stored cursor on, that is not finished; when none remains the plan is effectively exhausted. An entry whose origin is in `cancelled/` still stops with `terminal-lifecycle`, as #4129 does today. An entry with no lifecycle origin follows the stored cursor only.
2. No second record to keep in step. `scope:complete` and `scope:cancel` do not depend on the plan and are never rolled back for it. After a successful completion, `scope:complete` writes the stored cursor forward through the generation-locked store only when the checkout it runs in holds an untracked plan; it never writes a tracked plan file and never writes another checkout's plan. A failed or skipped write changes nothing else, because the reader derives. It prints one named line: `advanced`, `derived-only`, `no-sequence`, `no-entry`, `not-current` or `store-failed`.
3. One advance owner. The CLEAN-time `plan-sequence:advance` step leaves the review-cycle and pre-pr skills for entries that have a brief. The #4129 remediation text no longer raises the completed case, which is now the derived advance; it keeps the operator stop for the cancelled case.
4. Completion inheritance in `verify:plan-sequence`. Before the current-entry match, the verifier reads the outgoing change set itself: merge base to HEAD against the delivery branch, rename sources included; an empty or unreadable set gives no inheritance. It passes with the closed reason `completion-inherits-entry` only when all hold: at least one brief leaves `active/` or `pending/` and arrives in `completed/` with an unchanged intent digest (`extractIntentFromPayload` and `computeIntentDigest`, which omit only the known-machine keys); every brief path in the set is part of such a move; the only other paths are `CHANGELOG.md` and the spec-drift ledger; and every moved brief resolves from its own file to a plan entry at any status. A moved brief with no entry refuses as `completion-no-entry`. Every other change set, including one that only edits a planned brief or only touches the plan file, uses the ordinary current-entry rule. `pre-pr-controller/phases.ts` lists the new reason.
5. Approved insert. `plan-sequence:insert` adds one pending entry at the effective cursor or at a named later index. It needs a human-origin grant minted on a TTY through the existing `authz:grant` machinery (one new template), bound to the repository, `sequence_id`, generation, entry kind and id, and position, and usable once. The insert writes an approval row (entry id, grant id, time) under one new closed top-level key; entry keys are unchanged. `verify:plan-sequence` prints that row for the current entry.
6. No unapproved chain. `plan-sequence:set` in a checkout that already holds a plan file (live or exhausted) and `plan-sequence:clear` need the same grant class. So advancing a plan to its end and then replacing it adds nothing without an approval. A first `set` in a checkout with no plan file is unchanged.
7. Verification with the gate off in this repository. Unit regressions cover items 1 to 6: a completed brief with a stale stored cursor; a store failure during completion; an interrupted completion; a tracked plan (never written by completion); a linked worktree with no plan; a cancelled origin; a title-only match; a manual advance after a derived advance; a completion change set with an edited brief, with a changed intent digest, with a product path, with only the plan file, and for an issue with no entry; an insert without a grant; a grant reused for another entry; and advance-to-exhaustion followed by `set` without a grant. ## Summary

Under the bound pre-push gate, keeping the ordered plan (`.deft/plan-sequence.json`) current costs more than the delivery work. Three routine plan updates have no supported command, so every story ends in manual plan-sequence edits, or a human commits the plan outside the agent.

## What we saw (field report)

- A finished entry stays current until someone advances it, so the next push is refused.
- A completion PR needs its own plan entry.
- A bug fix that is not in the plan is refused, and there is no sanctioned way to add it.
- Cost: 82 plan-sequence commands in two days, and 64 `pre-pr:run` calls for 11 pushes.

## Asks

1. **Advance the plan on `scope:complete`.** When `scope:complete` succeeds for the brief named by the current entry, mark that entry completed and move the cursor to the next entry in the same operation. If the advance cannot be made (for example, the entry does not match the brief), refuse with a named reason. Never skip silently.
2. **A completion PR inherits its issue's plan entry.** A leftover-complete or lifecycle PR for issue N is admitted under the plan entry for issue N. It does not need a separate entry.
3. **A sanctioned path for an unplanned fix.** One command records the operator's approval and inserts the entry, at the cursor or at a named position. The approval is recorded and attributable. Head-authored text or narrative is not consent (see `content/docs/scope-provenance.md`). Without this command, the fix is refused as it is today.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Ask 1: after `scope:complete`, the next push of the next story is admitted with no manual plan-sequence command. A negative regression covers a mismatched entry.
- [ ] Ask 2: a completion PR for an issue with a plan entry is admitted with no new entry. A negative regression covers a PR for an issue that has no entry.
- [ ] Ask 3: an unplanned fix is admitted only after the approval command runs, and the recorded approval is visible to `verify:plan-sequence`.

## Out of scope (tracked elsewhere)

- Plan-only commit with no active brief: #5839
- Admitting every entry of a parallel cohort: #4433
- `pre-pr:run` as one command that runs and records all phases: #5933, #5977

## Related

- #4129 (closed): detects a current entry whose story is already finished. Ask 1 removes the need to recover from that state.
- #6025: re-enabling the bound pre-PR push gate in this repo.
